rationale: PGS002786 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly matches the target trait (bipolar disorder), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are subtype scores (bipolar I/II). All three are otherwise near-clones (same publication, SDPR method, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, similar covariates, no PRS-only AUC/R2, and only small partial R² reported in a non-diagnosis phenotyping context), so the small full-model/partial R² differences (highest in PGS002788) are not enough to outweigh the clearer endpoint label match of PGS002786. Confidence is low because phenotyping_reported fields for all candidates appear misaligned with a bipolar disorder diagnosis endpoint.

PGS000327 is the cleaner direct match to autism spectrum disorder across all endpoint fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ASD), comes from an ASD-focused GWAS meta-analysis publication, and shows stronger available performance proxies (full-model R² 0.0245 plus an OR=1.33 per SD) than PGS002790. While neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R², PGS002790 has a clear endpoint fidelity problem (phenotyping_reported is 'Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)' despite ASD labels) and its reported partial R² is much smaller (0.00546), making it less likely to rank well on external performance benchmarks despite its more modern shrinkage method and larger variant count.

PGS001033 is the only candidate that directly maps to the target umbrella trait (trait_efo = blood coagulation disease) and it provides clean PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and PGS-only R² 0.0578) with only basic covariates, plus broader multi-ancestry evaluation. The closest runner-up is PGS002034 (near-clone with PGS001826), which has a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoint (not the generic blood coagulation disease) and reports only partial correlation (~0.056) without AUROC/R², giving weaker performance evidence for external benchmark ranking; between the two near-clones, their metrics are essentially identical so neither clearly beats PGS001033.

All candidates are endpoint-aligned to asthma, but PGS001344 is the only one with clean PRS-only discrimination metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.64568; PGS-only R2=0.05973) under basic covariates, giving the strongest direct performance proxy for external benchmarking. The strongest runner-up is PGS001782 (same trait, genome-wide PRS-CS-auto) but it lacks PRS-only AUROC and shows lower PRS-comparable R2 (0.048844) with only a full-model AUROC (0.659) that is not directly comparable. The portability-paper scores (PGS002061/PGS001849) provide only partial correlation (~0.11–0.12) without PRS-only AUC/R2, making them less benchmark-informative than PGS001344 despite similar UKB-based endpoints.

All candidates are on-trait for ankylosing spondylitis, but PGS001268 has the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence in the shortlist: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.7346 and PGS-only R²=0.10232 (European validation), which are clean standalone PRS metrics and remain plausible under the provided heritability ceiling sanity-check. The closest runner-up is PGS001267 (same study family, same covariates, same variant count and validation context) but it is consistently slightly weaker on PRS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PRS-only R² (0.0988). The other candidates either lack PRS-only metrics and only provide weaker proxies (partial-r for PGS002089/PGS001876) or have a small EAS-only evaluation with only full-model AUROC and unknown covariates (PGS003420), making them less reliable for performance-oriented ranking.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, same publication (UKB portability framework), same training cohort/size, same covariates, same evaluation ancestries and validation N, and essentially identical partial correlation performance (0.0563 vs 0.0562). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 to separate them, the main differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally expected to capture more polygenic signal than an extremely sparse penalized regression score in this setting. The tiny partial-r edge also favors PGS002034, though it is negligible.

PGS001135 is the only candidate that is a direct match to the generic target trait (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported=Arthritis (nos)) and also reports clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R2=0.00291), which are sanity-consistent with the provided low heritability ceiling. The strongest runner-up for endpoint relevance is the Commun Biol ‘Other arthritis’ pair (PGS004547/PGS004477), but both lack any AUC/R2 and provide only modest per-SD ORs (1.26 and 1.20), giving weaker performance proxy evidence than PGS001135 despite their genome-wide variant counts. The RA/JIA scores (PGS004873, PGS000114) are more specific subtypes and rely on full-model/time-to-event metrics without PRS-only comparables, making them less direct matches for a generic ‘arthritis’ target.

All candidates map to COPD, but PGS001783 and PGS001788 are the closest endpoint matches (both explicitly COPD in trait_reported/phenotyping_reported) and share the same publication/method family (PRS-CS-auto, global biobank framework). Between these two near-clones, PGS001783 has materially stronger PRS-comparable performance (covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only R2=0.0381 vs 0.0163 for PGS001788) and higher reported AUROC (0.74 vs 0.715) with similarly basic covariates, and its PRS-only R2 aligns with the COPD heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.012; h2_liab≈0.039) without exceeding it. The snpnet UKB framework scores (PGS001332/333/334) have much weaker PRS-only metrics (R2≈0.002–0.003; PGS-only AUROC≈0.54) and include less direct/packaged endpoints (algorithmic-defined, time-to-event), so they are less likely to rank #1 on external performance benchmarks despite cleaner PGS-only AUROC reporting.

PGS004913 is the most direct, disease-focused match to the target: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis” with trait_efo exactly “alcoholic liver cirrhosis”, and it is presented as a dedicated PRS for alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers. Its covariates are clean/basic (age, sex, PCs) and it reports PRS-relevant effect separation (OR top vs bottom deciles = 4.4). The strongest runner-up on performance proxy is PGS000704 (full-model C-index 0.711, huge UKB sample), but it comes from a broad UKB framework-style paper and only provides a modest per-SD HR (1.18), with no PRS-only AUC/R2; its apparent advantage is largely study scale rather than disease-focused PRS evidence. PGS001777 has a higher top-vs-bottom effect (OR 6.18) but is a very sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates and a full-model AUROC (0.671) that is not PRS-comparable, making it less reliable as a standalone PRS than PGS004913.

All five candidates are direct matches to breast carcinoma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Breast cancer”), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), training N (12,483), evaluation ancestry mix, validation N (48,968), and similarly clean covariate field (“0”), so this is a near-clone comparison where performance/effect-size differences are the main differentiator. PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported discrimination among the shortlist: highest full-model AUROC (0.6625 vs 0.6598 for the closest runner-up PGS004040) and highest R² (0.0764 vs 0.0739), plus the largest per-SD OR (1.826 vs 1.809). Given identical endpoint and study context, this consistent edge across AUROC/R²/OR supports PGS004153 as the best-supported pick over the strongest runner-up (PGS004040).

Both candidates are exact matches for corneal dystrophy (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported identical), from the same UKB portability publication, with the same training size, covariates, ancestry evaluation mix, and validation sample size—so performance/structure differences are the main differentiators. PGS002042 shows higher reported partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384 for PGS001835) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is a favorable structural signal when endpoints are otherwise identical. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for either, the higher partial-r plus broader variant coverage gives PGS002042 the clearer edge over the strongest runner-up (PGS001835).

PGS005252 is the strongest direct-match aortic stenosis score in the shortlist: it has exact trait alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo) with a clear endpoint (“Incident aortic stenosis cases”), and it provides the most informative performance proxy available here (C-index/full-model AUC 0.87 plus HR 1.92) in a very large European validation (n=446,895). The main runner-up is PGS005254, which is also incident aortic stenosis with cleaner/basic covariates and larger training (n=205,483), but it lacks any AUC/C-index and shows a weaker effect size (HR 1.64). PGS005255/PGS005256 are less direct (valve-function measurements as reported traits) and also have weaker HR (~1.53), while PGS004911 is off-trait (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy).

All candidates map to celiac disease, but PGS000042/PGS000041 are explicitly restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (endpoint mismatch vs generic celiac disease) and have much lower AUROC (~0.72–0.73). The main competition is PGS000316 vs PGS000040 vs PGS001301. PGS001301 provides clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.8287; PGS-only R2 0.1422) but is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework phenotype (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), which is a known weaker archetype for external generalization despite tidy metrics. Between the two disease-focused direct celiac disease models, PGS000040 reports the strongest discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.90) on a direct celiac disease endpoint, exceeding PGS000316’s full-model AUROC 0.879; with no PRS-only metrics available for either, this within-trait performance edge is the best available proxy while maintaining endpoint fidelity.

PGS001263 is the only candidate with an exact atrial flutter endpoint across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, and it also provides clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617, PGS-only R2=0.025) with basic covariates, staying well below the heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0157; scale differences aside, no red-flag inflation). The strongest runner-up is PGS001339, which has very similar design and similarly clean PRS-only metrics but targets a broader time-to-event composite (atrial fibrillation and flutter) and has slightly weaker PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.613; R2 0.024). PGS002050 and PGS001841 are also broader AF+flutter portability-framework scores and lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r), giving weaker performance comparability for ranking.

All candidates are direct matches to cervical carcinoma with incident cervical cancer endpoints, but none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so selection falls back to structural/model-quality proxies and minimally packaged covariates. PGS003428 is from a disease-focused cervical-phenotypes GWAS meta-analysis and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (~2.9M), which is a strong structural predictor of external PRS performance versus the sparse GWAS-hit scores (PGS000073/PGS000784: 10 variants; PGS005165: 15 variants). Against the strongest runner-up (PGS000073/PGS000784), their higher full-model AUROC (~0.745) is likely driven by a much heavier covariate set (parity, oral contraceptive use, pack-years, etc.) and thus is less informative about standalone PRS strength; their per-SD HRs (~1.21–1.22) are also weaker than PGS003428’s HR (1.33). PGS003428’s full-model C-index (0.613) is lower, but with much lighter covariates (age, smoking) and stronger PRS effect size plus genome-wide construction, it is the better-supported choice for expected external benchmark performance.

PGS002032 and PGS001824 are the strongest direct matches: both target the exact same endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: "Disorders of bilirubin excretion"; trait_efo matches), come from the same UKB portability publication, share the same training size, ancestry distribution, covariates, and identical reported partial correlation (partial-r=0.0716). Between these near-clones, PGS002032 has a clear structural advantage with a far larger variant set (19,768 vs 22) using LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage, which is the most plausible proxy for better external benchmark performance when other fields are indistinguishable. PGS000924 reports very high PRS-only AUROC/R2, but it is a broader/mixed endpoint (porphyrin + bilirubin) and time-to-event, and it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper—both of which are warning signals versus the cleaner direct bilirubin-excretion endpoint siblings.

All candidates are direct matches for basal cell carcinoma with EUR-only evaluation and no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so we rely on within-family performance proxies and structural signals. Among the four near-clone Cancer PRSweb models (PGS000452/454/456/458) with identical endpoint, covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs1-4), training cohort (MGI), and validation size (n=11,322), PGS000454 has the best reported pseudo-R² (0.0489 vs 0.0487/0.0456/0.0457) while matching the top AUROC (0.632, tied with PGS000452) and showing a stronger top-1% vs rest OR (3.79) than PGS000452. The alternative outside this family, PGS000730, has slightly lower AUROC (0.624), unknown covariates, and lacks comparable supporting metrics beyond a per-SD OR, so it does not present a clear multi-field advantage over the best-performing PRSweb sibling.

All three candidates map to Crohn disease, but PGS004254 has the strongest visible performance proxy for external ranking: a much larger reported effect size (OR=2.18 per SD) and substantially higher discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.72 with only basic covariates: age/sex/PCs) than the snpnet framework scores. The main runner-up, PGS001331, provides clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.579, R2=0.00677) but comes from the pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework and shows modest PRS signal; its PRS-only R2 is also well below the trait heritability ceiling, consistent with weak predictive power. PGS001330 is additionally penalized by a time-to-event endpoint framing and slightly weaker metrics than PGS001331. Despite lacking PRS-only AUC/R2, PGS004254’s endpoint fidelity and markedly stronger effect-size/discrimination evidence give it the best-supported direct-match profile here.

All candidates are direct matches to abdominal aortic aneurysm, but PGS001784 is the only one with a clean PRS-comparable metric reported (pgs_only_r2=0.014661; also r2=0.014661), which is a strong proxy for external benchmark rank. Its PRS-only R2 is also plausible under the provided EUR liability heritability ceiling (~0.02), suggesting the metric is not inflated. The strongest runner-up is PGS003973 (same trait, disease-focused Nat Genet meta-analysis, PRS-CS) with a high full-model C-index (0.882) using only basic covariates, but it lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 so that discrimination is not directly attributable to the PRS and is less comparable for performance-oriented ranking. Other alternatives are weaker on performance evidence: PGS003972 reports only a modest full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates, PGS002054 is a portability-framework score with only a very small partial-r (0.0144), and PGS000753 is a sparse 29-variant P+T score with only an OR=1.37 per SD and no AUC/R2.

PGS002755 is the strongest direct-match eczema/atopic dermatitis PRS in the shortlist on structural and performance-proxy evidence: it targets incident atopic dermatitis (aligned to atopic eczema), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants (stronger polygenic capture than GWAS-hit scores), and shows a higher HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 versus the closest same-endpoint runner-up PGS004587 (HR 1.153) in the same large EUR evaluation setting (n=337,910) with identical covariates. The other candidates are weaker matches or less reliable: PGS003486/PGS003459 are therapy-specific paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (endpoint mismatch), and PGS001773 reports very high full-model AUROC/R2 in a tiny validation (n=676) for moderate-to-severe AD with ethnicity covariates, making its discrimination less comparable and likely inflated relative to standalone PRS performance.

PGS004546 is the strongest direct match: it targets ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis with matching trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, and comes from the same Commun Biol study family as the top-ranked sibling but uses an explicit multi-score aggregation approach (RFDiseasemetaPRS) rather than a single-score LDpred2. With no candidates reporting PRS-only AUC/R2, the best available performance proxy is the per-SD effect size; PGS004546 shows a higher OR (1.2986) than the closest runner-up PGS004476 (OR 1.2194) under the same endpoint, ancestry (EUR-only dev/eval), cohorts (UKB), and validation size (n=56,192), making it the better-supported likely higher-performing model. The portability-framework options (PGS002072/PGS001861) are on a broader composite endpoint (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) and, despite reporting partial-r (~0.095–0.098), are framework-derived and not clearly superior to the disease-focused K80 models; PGS005150 is EAS-evaluated only and less aligned to the EUR heritability context provided.

All top candidates are broadly on-target for dementia, but PGS004281 is the strongest performance-proxy direct match: it targets all-cause dementia (trait_efo=dementia; phenotyping_reported=All-cause dementia) and reports the highest available discrimination (full-model AUROC≈0.819) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PC1-10) in a large evaluation sample (n=67,428 EUR). The closest runner-up is its near-clone sibling PGS004284 (same paper/endpoint/covariates/ancestry), which has essentially identical but very slightly lower AUROC and pseudo-R2, so PGS004281 wins on within-family metric edge. PGS005170 is also endpoint-faithful but its reported AUROC (0.761) is lower and it includes APOE allele dosage as a covariate (less comparable to standalone PRS), while PGS000823/PGS000812 are Alzheimer’s-focused sparse scores with weaker/less complete performance evidence.

All candidates are direct CAD matches and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so the best proxy is effect-size strength within the strongest disease-focused study family. PGS003725/PGS003726/PGS003727 are near-clone siblings from the same 2023 Nat Med multi-ancestry CAD PRS paper with similar basic covariates; among them, PGS003725 shows the strongest reported discrimination proxies (HR 1.75 and OR 2.14 per SD) versus PGS003726 (HR 1.73 only) and PGS003727 (HR 1.67). Compared with the main runner-up outside this family (PGS002244, OR 1.64) and the older PGS000018 (prevalent CAD; full-model AUROC 0.89 is not PRS-comparable and training n is very small), PGS003725 has the clearest advantage in effect-size magnitude while retaining clean endpoint fidelity and broad multi-ancestry evaluation.

All candidates are direct atrial fibrillation matches, so the decision turns on performance proxies and packaging/covariate cleanliness. PGS005313 shows the strongest PRS signal proxy among the top contenders with a high per-SD effect size (OR=1.82 with tight CI) and a solid AUROC=0.78 under relatively light covariates (age, sex), plus a modern cross-population PRS-CSx construction with very large genome-wide coverage (1,271,239 variants) and multi-ancestry GWAS input. The main runner-up, PGS005168, reports a much higher C-index (0.8718) but it is explicitly bundled with the CHARGE-AF clinical risk calculator (covariates include CHARGE-AF), making the full-model discrimination heavily non-comparable to standalone PRS performance; it also lacks any PRS-only AUC/R2. Compared with older LDpred scores (PGS000016/PGS000331) and the P+T score (PGS002814), PGS005313 has stronger effect-size evidence and more methodologically/structurally favorable genome-wide modeling without obvious clinical-risk packaging.

PGS002237 is the most direct, disease-focused CKD score in the shortlist with strong endpoint specificity (CKD stage 3+; eGFR <45) and explicit multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/ASN/EUR/MAE), which is supportive for external robustness. While it lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, its reported per-SD effect size is the strongest among the broadly applicable CKD candidates (OR 1.47 vs 1.35 for PGS005113 and 1.15 for PGS002757), and it comes from a CKD-focused Nat Med study designed to predict CKD across ancestries. The main runner-up is PGS005090, which shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.90) and reports R²=0.10, but that R² is not labeled PRS-only and the AUROC is likely covariate-inflated; additionally it is ancestry-restricted (AFR-only GWAS/EVAL), making it less reliable as the single best general CKD match when target ancestry is unspecified. PGS004889 is penalized by endpoint restriction (incident CKD without diabetes) and clinical risk-score packaging in covariates.

PGS002738 is the most direct match to the target (trait_efo exactly alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported alcohol use disorder) and has the strongest visible discriminative proxy among the direct AUD candidates: OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (vs 1.76 for PGS002739). It also uses a genome-wide PRS-CS score with substantial variant count (326k), whereas PGS002739 is a much sparser gene-based score (858 variants) and is evaluated only in AFR, making it less broadly comparable for a generic alcohol dependence target. The main runner-up is PGS002739 due to same endpoint fidelity, but it has weaker OR evidence and a more restricted evaluation context. PGS000201/PGS000202 are less endpoint-faithful (problematic alcohol use / dependence measurement) and show smaller incremental R2, so they are less likely to rank best on external performance for alcohol dependence.

PGS004621 is the strongest direct match to the target (trait_efo = cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported = Cirrhosis) and has the most performance-predictive structural profile: a genome-wide PRS-CS score with ~1.09M variants developed across multiple large biobanks, consistent with better external benchmark performance than sparse GWAS-hit scores. Its reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.68 with only basic covariates age/sex/PCs) is comparable to other cirrhosis-labeled candidates while avoiding the endpoint mismatches seen in the main runner-up set (PGS000704/PGS001777/PGS000776 are alcohol-related/incident-at-risk formulations). Versus the closest same-trait runner-up PGS000726 (also cirrhosis of liver), PGS004621 has a clear methodological/coverage advantage (PRS-CS genome-wide vs 12 SNPs) and much broader multi-cohort development/validation context, making it the better-supported choice despite both lacking PRS-only AUC/R2.

All candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy, but PGS004949 has the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence among the closest siblings: it reports a higher univariate (PRS-only) AUC (0.68) than the other multi-ancestry Nat Genet siblings (PGS004951 PRS-only AUC 0.67; PGS004947 0.66) and similarly strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.91). Its evaluation is large (n=326,106) and uses only basic covariates, while the top-ranked prior (PGS004862) lacks PRS-only metrics and only provides full-model AUROC/R², which are not comparable as standalone PRS performance. Therefore PGS004949 is the best-supported direct-match candidate versus the strongest runner-up PGS004951.

All candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris, but PGS001262 has the strongest clean PRS-only performance evidence among the shortlist (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683; PGS-only R² 0.01304), edging the closest same-study snpnet siblings PGS001261 (0.58233; 0.01228) and PGS001260 (0.58108; 0.01185). It also avoids the time-to-event endpoint framing of PGS001261 and has a larger validation sample than the other snpnet siblings. The MVP ldpred PheCode models (PGS005048/PGS005052) report only full-model C-index (no PRS-only AUC/R²), making their apparent performance less comparable for PRS ranking despite similar covariates; thus the best-supported PRS-direct metric winner is PGS001262. Heritability sanity-check is passed (PGS-only R² ~0.013 below h2_obs ~0.009–0.014 range, close but not implausibly above given scale differences), supporting metric plausibility.

All candidates are on-trait for major depressive disorder, but the three near-clone scores from the same bioRxiv study (PGS003580/PGS003578/PGS003576) are directly comparable (same endpoint wording, same method PRSice-2, same covariates PCs 1-10, same training cohort UKB, same validation size n=42,250 and EUR-selected record). Within this near-clone family, PGS003578 has the strongest reported variance explained (full_model_r2=0.0257) versus PGS003580 (0.0254) and PGS003576 (0.0241), making it the best performance proxy available in this shortlist. The top-ranked prior PGS002759 has only an OR per SD (1.26, modest) and no R2/AUC, and PGS003333 reports a lower pseudo-R2 (0.022) with unknown covariates, so neither has a clearer multi-field advantage over the best-performing near-clone.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, covariates, training cohort (UKB), training N, ancestry distribution, and validation N; neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. The only differentiators are performance proxy and structural properties: PGS002031 has a slightly higher partial correlation (0.1355 vs 0.1307) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with many more variants (6713 vs 654), which is a favorable structural signal for polygenic disease prediction. Given the otherwise identical context, these small but consistent advantages make PGS002031 the best-supported direct match over PGS001823.

PGS000997 is the strongest direct-match on diverticular disease with the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PRS-only AUROC=0.591 and PRS-only R²=0.0178 on European validation, with standard non-leaky covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). The closest runner-up, PGS004614, has excellent phenotype alignment but only a full-model AUROC=0.76 and includes family history as a covariate, making its discrimination less attributable/comparable to the PRS itself; it also lacks PRS-only metrics. The other candidates (PGS004544/PGS004474) provide only modest per-SD ORs (~1.31) without AUC/R², and PGS000996 has weaker PRS-only metrics and a broader mixed endpoint (diverticular disease/diverticulitis).

All three candidates are direct phenotype matches for Dupuytren contracture, but PGS001254 is the only one with explicit PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6646; PGS-only R²=0.02466) plus incremental AUROC reported, giving the cleanest and strongest visible proxy for external benchmark ranking. The top-ranked portability-study options (PGS002092/PGS001880) provide only partial-correlation (~0.08) and no PRS-only AUROC/R², making their comparative performance harder to support despite similar endpoint wording and broader multi-ancestry evaluation. Between the two portability siblings, PGS002092 is only marginally higher partial-r than PGS001880, but neither has enough metric evidence to outweigh PGS001254’s directly comparable PRS-only discrimination.

All three candidates are direct matches to Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (same trait_efo and phenotyping_reported: lymphocytic thyroiditis) from the same publication family with the same evaluation ancestry mix and validation N, and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC). In this near-clone setting, the strongest PRS-quality proxy is the per-SD effect size: PGS005271 shows the strongest OR (1.55) and beta (0.44), indicating materially stronger genetic discrimination than PGS005270 (OR 1.04) and PGS005272 (OR 1.42). Although PGS005270 has a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.639 vs 0.630), small full-model AUROC differences are not reliable PRS differentiators here, so PGS005271’s stronger effect-size evidence makes it the best-supported choice.

PGS002304 is the strongest direct match on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both follicular lymphoma, consistent with trait_efo) and it also has the best available discrimination proxy in this shortlist (full-model AUROC 0.61, CI 0.59–0.63). The closest runner-up on phenotype is PGS003455 (trait_reported follicular lymphoma) but it has an explicit phenotype incoherence (phenotyping_reported = chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and provides only a weak per-SD OR (1.07) with no AUROC/R2, making it less supported. The PRSweb candidates (PGS000644/PGS000643) map to follicular lymphoma via trait_efo but are labeled/phenotyped as nodular lymphoma and show materially lower full-model AUROC (~0.53–0.54), so they do not outweigh PGS002304’s better endpoint alignment plus higher reported discrimination.

PGS000639 is the strongest direct-match: it has coherent endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all Hodgkin’s disease/lymphoma) and, within the near-clone PRSweb sibling set (PGS000638/637/640 share the same cohorts, EUR-only ancestry, covariates, and validation n=775), it shows the best available performance proxies (highest full-model AUROC 0.62 and highest Nagelkerke R² 0.0276, plus the strongest per-SD OR 1.476). The main runner-up is PGS000638, which is similarly aligned but has weaker discrimination (AUROC 0.601, R² 0.0193, OR 1.377). PGS003449 is excluded from contention despite the label because its phenotyping_reported is clearly mismatched (chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and it provides weak effect size evidence (OR ~1.02) with no AUC/R².

PGS000708 is the only candidate with an exact kidney-failure trait label (trait_reported and trait_efo both kidney failure) and it provides the strongest visible performance proxy in the shortlist (C-index/full-model 0.779) alongside a non-trivial per-SD effect size (HR 1.19). The main runner-up for endpoint relevance is the N18 chronic renal failure pair (PGS004562/PGS004492), but they provide no AUC/C-index and only modest ORs (1.40 and 1.17), giving weaker performance evidence. PGS002237 and PGS004158 are CKD (not kidney failure) endpoints; despite PGS002237’s similar full-model AUROC (0.78) and stronger OR (1.47), its phenotype is stage-3+ CKD with heavier clinical covariates, making it a less direct match to kidney failure than PGS000708.

All candidates are broadly on-trait for glaucoma, with several specifically targeting primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). PGS001792 has the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports a covariates-regressed-out (PRS-only) Nagelkerke R2=0.03209, which is interpretable and below the glaucoma liability h2 ceiling provided (0.0556), supporting metric plausibility. It also has a strong full-model AUROC (0.777) with only basic demographic/PC covariates (no family history/biomarker packaging), and a large validation sample (n=347,396). The strongest runner-up is PGS004944, which has very large validation (n=407,667) and a strong per-SD OR=1.74, but it lacks any PRS-only AUC/R2 and its reported AUROC=0.748 is full-model only, making it less predictive for external benchmark ranking than PGS001792’s explicit PRS-comparable R2. PGS000137’s AUROC=0.8 is undermined by inclusion of family history in covariates (risk-package leakage), and PGS001797 is a near-clone framework sibling with slightly lower PRS-only R2 and much smaller validation (n=7,128).

PGS004911 is the strongest direct-match HCM candidate in the shortlist: it has exact trait_efo/phenotyping_reported alignment to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~374k), and comes from the same disease-focused Nat Genet 2025 evaluation study family with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) rather than clinical risk-factor packaging. Versus the closest runner-up PGS004910 (same study, same endpoint, same covariates, similar variant count), PGS004911 shows materially better reported performance proxies in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.80 and R² 0.048 vs 0.73 and 0.031) and slightly stronger effect sizes (e.g., HR 2.34 vs 1.97), making it the better-supported likely top performer among near-clone siblings. Older alternatives are weaker: PGS000739 uses only 27 GWAS-significant variants and includes heavy clinical covariates/rare-variant carrier status (less comparable), and PGS000778 has a mismatched phenotyping context (events among pathogenic variant carriers) with tiny validation (n=368) and no discrimination metrics.

PGS000114 is the only candidate that directly matches the target umbrella trait “juvenile idiopathic arthritis” across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, whereas PGS000324/PGS000325/PGS000326 are subtype-specific endpoints (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular). All four are from the same disease-focused publication, same method (SparSNP), same basic covariates (sex, PCs 1–10), and EUR-only development/evaluation, so endpoint fidelity is the main differentiator. Although PGS000324 reports a much higher full-model AUROC (0.93) than PGS000114 (0.738), none report PRS-only AUC/R2, and full-model AUROC is not a reliable substitute; given the subtype mismatch and likely non-comparability of that outlier AUROC, the direct JIA score (PGS000114) is the best-supported match for the generic target trait.

All candidates are near-clones for the target (heart failure) with identical endpoint framing (PheCode 428.1 CHF NOS), same covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), same training cohort (MVP), same validation size (n=31,804) and similar ancestry context; none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we fall back to within-family performance proxies. PGS005083 has the highest reported full-model C-index/AUC (0.75368) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.455) among the shortlist, giving it a small but consistent edge over the closest runner-up PGS005077 (0.75358; OR 1.452). Given the tiny metric gaps and lack of PRS-only metrics, confidence is moderate.

All candidates are on-trait (hypertension), but PGS004236 and PGS004234 form the strongest disease-focused, multi-cohort Nat Commun cluster with multi-ancestry evaluation (European, African American/Afro-Caribbean, Hispanic/Latin American, Asian unspecified) and large validation (n=39,035). Between these near-clones (same publication, endpoint = prevalent hypertension, similar covariates including age/sex/PCs plus standard epidemiologic factors), PGS004236 has a marginally higher full-model AUROC (0.764 vs 0.763) and uniquely reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.1), providing additional PRS-strength evidence that PGS004234 lacks. The framework-style UKB sparse score PGS001320 has clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.629; R2 0.0649) but comes from a pan-trait pipeline and is less supported for external generalization than the disease-focused multi-cohort Nat Commun models; the other UKB-only models (PGS004934, PGS004193) have lower full-model AUROC and weaker/less complete evidence. Therefore PGS004236 is the best-supported direct-match candidate.

For target hyperthyroidism, the Graves’ disease scores (PGS005265/5266/5264) are acceptable direct matches because Graves’ is the dominant clinical cause of hyperthyroidism, and they come from a disease-focused multi-biobank study with broad external evaluation (MAE; n=94,651) rather than the pan-trait UKB framework (PGS001042/001043). Among the Graves’ near-clones, PGS005265 has the strongest visible performance proxy (highest reported full-model AUROC 0.6652 vs 0.6637 for PGS005266 and 0.6587 for PGS005264) and the strongest effect-size signal (OR per SD 1.63 vs 1.54 and ~1.01), while sharing essentially the same endpoint and evaluation context. The UKB snpnet models do report clean PGS-only AUC/R2 (~0.634; R2~0.022–0.024), but they are from a known pan-trait sparse framework and include a time-to-event packaging for PGS001042; given the domain guidance that disease-focused multi-cohort models typically outperform such framework scores when endpoint alignment is acceptable, PGS005265 is the best-supported pick.

All candidates are near-clones for the target trait (myocardial infarction PheCode 411.2; EFO myocardial infarction; phenotyping_reported myocardial infarction), from the same publication family, with the same basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), same training cohort (MVP), same ancestry distribution, and same validation sample size (n=30,379). None reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the best available performance proxy is the selected European full-model C-index/AUC plus per-SD OR. PGS005039 has the highest reported full-model C-index (0.78484) and the strongest OR (1.578) among the shortlist, giving it a small but consistent empirical edge over the closest runner-up PGS005045 (C-index 0.78385; OR 1.554).

PGS002082 is the top-ranked candidate and is a direct concept match to the target (trait_efo=lupus erythematosus; trait/phenotyping_reported="Lupus (localized and systemic)"). Versus the strongest runner-up PGS001870 (same UKB portability study, same endpoint wording, same covariates and evaluation setting), PGS002082 shows better reported PRS signal in the selected record via higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0212 vs 0.0184) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (361,553 vs 87), which is a favorable structural proxy when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent for both. The disease-focused SLE scores (PGS000328/PGS000754/PGS000196) have narrower or shifted endpoints (e.g., early-onset SLE, arthritis-clinic diagnosis) and only full-model AUROC (not PRS-only), making them less directly comparable for generic lupus erythematosus risk despite some higher AUROC values.

All candidates are on-trait (hypothyroidism), but PGS005218’s very high AUROC=0.859 is a full-model metric with heavy near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti‑TPO) in covariates, making it largely non-comparable and likely covariate-driven rather than PRS-driven. Among the remaining direct-match options, the 2022 Nat Genet sibling set (PGS002653/PGS002336/PGS002702) shares the same endpoint and covariates and reports incremental R2; within this near-clone family, PGS002653 has the strongest reported incremental R2 (0.0262 vs 0.0247 and 0.0206), making it the best performance proxy under comparable design. PGS004935 is from a portability/framework-style paper with sparse variants and only modest full-model AUROC=0.70 (covariates unknown), so it is less compelling than the best-performing sibling in the coherent Nat Genet cluster.

PGS002763 is the most direct match to the target (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Hip osteoarthritis”, EFO matches) and shows the strongest standalone PRS signal among the shortlist via effect size (OR=1.38 per SD, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.05M variants) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical). The strongest runner-up is PGS002728, which is hip-OA-related but uses a treatment/proxy endpoint (“Total hip replacement”) and a sparse 44-variant GWS score; its reported AUROC=0.66 is a full-model metric (age, sex) and not PRS-only, making it less reliable as a performance proxy than the stronger PRS effect-size evidence plus endpoint fidelity in PGS002763. Other candidates (PGS004478/PGS004548) have weaker ORs and unknown covariates, and PGS004882 is a framework-style incident/time-to-event package with modest C-index (0.60) despite large validation.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical endpoint alignment to the target (trait_efo=nicotine dependence; phenotyping_reported/trait_reported=Tobacco use disorder), similar covariates, training cohort/size, and validation size. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for either, the best differentiator is the within-study comparable performance proxy: PGS002037 has higher partial correlation (partial-r=0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), and it also uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), consistent with stronger polygenic signal capture. Therefore PGS002037 is better supported than the strongest runner-up (PGS001830).

All candidates are on-trait (melanoma, EFO melanoma) and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we fall back to endpoint fidelity plus the strongest available performance proxies. PGS000813 shows the strongest discrimination evidence in the shortlist with a higher reported AUROC (0.77, 0.75–0.79) and strong effect-size signals (OR per SD 2.12; OR top 10% vs middle 20% 5.7), with only basic covariates (age, sex) and a large multi-cohort development context. The closest runner-up, PGS000743, has a lower AUROC (0.74) and uses a much heavier covariate set including family history and multiple traditional risk factors, making its full-model AUROC less informative about PRS strength. The Br J Dermatol incident-invasive melanoma scores (PGS002247/PGS002246) have cleaner covariates but materially lower AUROC (~0.69). Therefore PGS000813 is the best-supported direct-match candidate.

All candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis, but none reports a clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must lean on the best available performance proxies plus study archetype. PGS002726 (ranked #1 prior) comes from a disease-focused MS susceptibility paper and shows the strongest visible discrimination/effect evidence in its selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.80 with a very large top-decile vs median OR=15.0), outperforming the closest disease-focused runner-up PGS000809 (full-model AUROC 0.765; R² 0.069). The UKB portability-framework scores (PGS002038/PGS001831) provide only weak partial-r (~0.04) and are penalized as framework-derived despite large UKB development, and PGS004699 is tied to an optic neuritis presentation context (risk-packaging-adjacent) with lower AUROC (0.752). Given comparable endpoint labels across the shortlist, PGS002726 has the clearest performance edge over the strongest runner-up (PGS000809) while avoiding the framework penalty.

All candidates are direct matches for gout (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align). None report clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we fall back to within-endpoint performance proxies and structural signals. Among the strongest comparable cluster (PGS004160/PGS004047/PGS004018 from the same Am J Hum Genet five-biobank evaluation with covariates=0 and identical training/validation context), PGS004160 is the ensemble MultiPRS and has the best reported discrimination/effect-size in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.694 and OR 2.05) versus the closest runner-up PGS004047 (AUROC 0.685, OR 2.00) and PGS004018 (AUROC 0.678, OR 1.93). PGS004265 shows a much higher full-model AUROC (0.798) but it is covariate-adjusted (age/sex/PCs) with no PRS-only metric and a low covariate-adjusted pseudo-R2 (0.040), making that AUROC less interpretable as PRS strength; PGS004768 reports only incremental R2 without a directly comparable PRS-only metric and has smaller validation. Therefore the best-supported direct-match pick is PGS004160.

Both candidates are direct matches to the target trait (ICD10 J33; EFO Nasal Cavity Polyp), from the same publication, with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (174,489), evaluation ancestry (EUR), validation N (56,192), and variant count (1,059,939). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 or full-model AUC/R2, so performance must be inferred from the available effect size. PGS004535 shows a materially stronger per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.6007) than PGS004465 (OR=1.3496), which is a meaningful proxy for stronger discriminative PRS signal within an otherwise near-clone context. Although PGS004465 uses LDpred2 (a strong shrinkage method), the domain guidance prioritizes within-family empirical performance signals over method labels when endpoints and context are the same; thus PGS004535 is better supported.

All candidates are direct kidney-cancer matches (renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma; several are incident kidney cancer). None report clean PGS-only AUC/R2, so we fall back to the strongest performance proxies and structural evidence. PGS004908 has the best visible discrimination proxy (full-model AUROC 0.74 with CI 0.72–0.75) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.5, 1.43–1.58), exceeding the HR~1.15–1.16 seen in the closest runner-ups (PGS000076/PGS000787) despite similar covariate sets. It is also supported by a large, disease-focused multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) and uses substantially more GWAS-significant variants (107 vs 19), consistent with capturing more signal. Compared with PGS000076 (AUROC 0.722; HR 1.16) and PGS000787 (same AUROC; HR 1.15), PGS004908 shows a clear multi-field advantage in effect size and AUROC while remaining endpoint-faithful.

All candidates are broadly on-trait for lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia, but PGS000788 and PGS000077 are the closest near-clone pair: same reported trait and phenotyping (incident lymphocytic leukemia), same 75-variant GWAS-hits construction lineage, same basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), and same EUR evaluation context with identical large validation sample size (n=391,338). In that like-for-like setting, PGS000788 shows consistently stronger visible performance proxies than PGS000077 (higher full-model AUROC 0.738 vs 0.719; higher C-index 0.756 vs 0.735; stronger per-SD HR 1.70 vs 1.45). Other candidates have materially weaker discrimination evidence and/or much smaller validation (e.g., PGS000645 AUROC 0.578; PGS002305 AUROC 0.57; PGS003453 lacks AUROC/R2 and is CLL-specific). Although none report clean PGS-only AUC/R2 (and the R²=0.415 in PGS000788 is likely not PRS-only and is heritability-inconsistent), the within-family metric advantage and stronger effect size make PGS000788 the best-supported direct-match pick.

All candidates are direct lung cancer matches, but most report only covariate-augmented (full-model) AUROC with no PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must use the best available performance proxy while checking for packaging/leakage. PGS004860 is endpoint-faithful (incident lung cancer) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2; 1,143,554 variants), and it shows the strongest visible discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.893, CI 0.887–0.898) plus a moderate per-SD effect size (OR 1.33). The strongest runner-up is PGS000078/PGS000789 (near-clones with identical covariates and AUROC 0.846; HR ~1.16–1.17) but they are heavily packaged with many non-genetic predictors (family history, detailed smoking variables and interactions, PM2.5), making their full-model AUROC less informative about PRS strength; their effect sizes are also weaker than PGS004860’s. PGS000740 is an early-onset (<50) endpoint mismatch for generic lung cancer, and PGS000721 has much lower AUROC (0.738) and very small validation. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics across the set, PGS004860’s combination of genome-wide construction and best available performance proxy makes it the most likely top external performer.

PGS004606 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused AMD score in the shortlist: it targets age-related macular degeneration with matching EFO/phenotyping, uses a genome-wide PRS-CS model (~1.0M variants), and shows strong PRS signal via OR=1.76 per SD with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) in a large European validation (n=163,011). The closest runner-up is PGS004952, which reports a higher full-model AUROC (~0.842) but is evaluated on a much smaller sample (n=1,232) and its endpoint is specifically late AMD under a particular clinical classification system, making it less directly aligned to the generic target and its high AUROC less reliable as a PRS-performance proxy. PGS004607 is from the same Nat Genet family but has weaker performance proxies (AUROC 0.65, OR 1.48) and a GWAS ancestry mismatch (AFR-only GWAS with EUR eval). The UKB framework/portability scores (PGS001013, PGS002041) have weaker phenotype fidelity and/or much weaker PRS signal metrics.

All candidates map to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease by trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS002289 is endpoint-mismatched (cognitive test performance interaction rather than LOAD diagnosis), and PGS004918 has only a small evaluation (n=136) with a full-model AUROC (0.731) that is not PRS-only and thus weakly comparable. PGS000054 vs the strongest runner-up PGS000053 are near-clones from the same Neurology study (same 21 GWAS-significant variants, same familial LOAD phenotyping, same basic covariates age/sex, same development cohorts); the main differentiator is effect size, where PGS000054 shows a materially stronger OR per SD (1.73 vs 1.29), which is a meaningful proxy for better standalone PRS discrimination in the absence of PRS-only AUC/R2 across the shortlist. PGS000334 reports an R²=0.191 but it appears to be a generic/full-model variance-explained metric with unknown covariates and is implausibly high relative to the provided heritability ceiling, making it less reliable as a performance proxy than the strong OR evidence in PGS000054.

PGS005262 is the best direct match to the target trait (nodular goiter): both trait_reported and trait_efo are explicitly “Benign nodular goiter / benign, nodular goiter,” whereas PGS005273 and PGS005274 are case-control contrasts for “thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter” (off-target because the endpoint is cancer discrimination, not goiter risk). Among the three benign nodular goiter models (PGS005262, PGS005263, PGS005261), all share the same study family, evaluation setting (MAE; n=94,651), and lack PRS-only metrics; within this near-clone set PGS005262 has the strongest visible performance proxies (highest full-model AUROC 0.5933 and highest per-SD effect size OR 1.41) compared with PGS005263 (AUROC 0.5876; OR 1.36) and PGS005261 (AUROC 0.5854; OR ~1.05, much weaker).

All candidates are direct matches for multiple myeloma (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported; EUR evaluation), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot rank on clean PRS-comparable metrics. The main differentiator is comparability/cleanliness of the reported performance context: PGS002281 reports a full-model AUROC=0.644 with explicitly basic covariates (age, sex, geographic region), plus a strong extreme-quantile effect (OR highest vs lowest quintile 3.18), and has a substantially larger validation sample (n=2,395). The strongest runner-up is PGS002306 with higher full-model AUROC=0.69, but it is based on a much smaller validation (n=290) and has unknown covariates, making that AUROC less interpretable/comparable. The PRSweb scores (PGS000653/654/652) have clearly lower AUROC (~0.55–0.58) and modest per-SD ORs (~1.24–1.33), so they are less likely to top an external performance benchmark among same-trait options.

Among the shortlist, PGS001274 and PGS001273 are the only candidates with clean PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2). Between these near-clone siblings (same snpnet framework paper, same training cohort/size, same covariates, same validation size/ancestry context), PGS001274 has consistently stronger PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.57595 vs 0.5685; R2 0.00945 vs 0.00688) and higher incremental AUROC (0.00777 vs 0.00477), making it the better performance proxy. The other candidates (PGS004565/PGS004560/PGS002768) lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and report only modest per-SD ORs (~1.31–1.33) with unknown or non-informative covariate/metric context, so they provide weaker benchmark-oriented evidence despite acceptable trait labels.

All candidates are on-trait (knee osteoarthritis / gonarthrosis) and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so selection falls back to endpoint fidelity + structural PRS strength proxies (method/variant count, effect size) rather than full-model metrics. PGS002767 is an exact knee osteoarthritis endpoint with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical) and a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) using ~1.05M variants, with a moderate per-SD OR=1.35. The strongest runner-up is the Commun Biol pair (PGS004549/PGS004479), which are also genome-wide (~1.06M) but have unknown covariates and slightly weaker ORs (1.37 and 1.32) with a risk-factor-integration study archetype that can imply packaging/complexity; between them, PGS004549 has the higher OR but still lacks covariate clarity. PGS002729 and PGS004883 provide only full-model AUROC/C-index (0.66/0.60) with additional covariates or incident/time-to-event framing, which are not reliable PRS-comparable advantages here. Given comparable effect sizes, PGS002767’s cleaner covariate disclosure and direct disease-focused framing make it the best-supported direct-match choice.

Both candidates map to psoriatic arthritis (same trait_efo), but PGS001287 has substantially stronger and cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.676 and PGS-only R2=0.0335 (no-covariates), whereas PGS000342 reports only a low full-model AUROC=0.562 with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics. PGS001287 also has much larger training/validation and broader evaluation ancestry coverage. Although PGS001287 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a negative archetype signal), its direct PRS-only metrics and markedly better discrimination than PGS000342 make it the best-supported direct-match in this shortlist.

All candidates are broadly on-trait for obesity, but PGS005235 has the strongest visible PRS-strength proxy while maintaining good endpoint fidelity: despite the broader label (“Adiposity”), its phenotyping is explicitly obesity (phecode 278.1) with only basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and it shows a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97) than the closest EUR direct-label runner-up PGS004447 (OR≈1.36, covariates unknown). Compared with the portability/framework-style PGS002033 (partial-r≈0.079 in a UKB portability paper), PGS005235 is more disease-endpoint anchored and shows markedly stronger discrimination proxy. The EAS-only models (PGS005154/PGS005145) are less comparable for a generic obesity target absent an EAS deployment context, and their betas are harder to compare directly to the EUR OR evidence.

Both candidates are direct matches to otosclerosis (trait_efo=otosclerosis), but PGS001255 provides the cleanest, most benchmark-relevant PRS-only performance evidence: PGS-only AUROC=0.6319 and PGS-only R2=0.01341 in European validation, with basic covariates and metrics that are plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0048; scale differences aside, nothing is implausibly inflated). In contrast, PGS002046 (portability framework) reports no PRS-only AUROC/R2 and only a small partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182), which is a weaker and less directly comparable proxy for external ranking. Despite PGS002046 using a genome-wide shrinkage method and many variants, the lack of PRS-comparable discrimination metrics makes it less well-supported than PGS001255 for performance-oriented selection.

All candidates are direct matches for ovarian neoplasm (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), from the same publication family, with identical ancestry context (EUR-only), cohorts (UKB), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and validation size—so this is a near-clone comparison where performance proxies can break ties. PGS000550 has the strongest visible performance among the shortlist (highest full-model AUROC 0.568 and highest Nagelkerke R² 0.0113) and also the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.286 vs 1.263 for the closest runner-up PGS000549). With no PRS-only AUC/R² reported for any candidate, these within-family differences plus the genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) support PGS000550 over PGS000549 and the weaker siblings (PGS000551/560/564).

All five candidates are near-clones for the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all T1D; same publication, cohorts, ancestry distribution, training n=804, validation n=90,274, and covariates=0), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the best available differentiator is within-family performance/effect size. PGS004162 has the highest reported AUROC (0.771 vs 0.758 for the strongest runner-up PGS004078) and the highest R² (0.141 vs 0.124), along with the strongest OR per SD (2.89 vs 2.68), making it the best-supported pick in this otherwise matched set.

PGS001280 is the best direct-match to the target trait (pulmonary embolism) with coherent endpoint fields (trait_efo=pulmonary embolism; phenotyping_reported=TTE PE) and clean PRS-only performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.60765; PGS-only R2=0.01403) under basic covariates, with multi-ancestry evaluation listed. The strongest runner-up is PGS001277, which has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2 (0.61144/0.01508) but is a composite endpoint (PE +/- DVT) rather than PE-specific, reducing endpoint fidelity for a PE-only target. PGS003861 has an exact PE label but reports only a full-model AUROC (0.765) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics, making its apparent advantage non-comparable to the PRS-only evidence available for PGS001280.

All candidates map to psoriasis, but PGS001312 is the strongest direct-match on comparable PRS performance evidence: it reports clean PRS-only AUROC=0.6916 and PRS-only R²=0.0523 with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), and uses the non–time-to-event psoriasis endpoint. The closest runner-up is its near-clone sibling PGS001313 from the same pan-trait UKB framework, but PGS001313 is time-to-event (phenotyping_reported: TTE psoriasis) and has clearly lower PRS-only AUROC (0.6729) and R² (0.0497). The portability-framework scores (PGS002083/PGS001871) lack PRS-only AUC/R² and only provide partial-r (~0.063), and PGS002293 is a small GWS-variant lifestyle-integration study without comparable PRS discrimination metrics, so neither has stronger benchmark-oriented performance proxies than PGS001312.

All candidates are broadly on-trait for pancreatic carcinoma, but PGS002264 is a subtype (pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) and its very high AUROC=0.83 is from a clinically packaged model including diabetes status/onset and family history (“clinical risk”), making that performance non-comparable to a standalone PRS. Among the remaining direct pancreatic cancer models, PGS000083 and PGS000794 are near-clones (same 22-variant basis, same endpoint ‘incident pancreatic cancer’, same covariates, and essentially identical AUROC/C-index and HR). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available to separate them and no clear multi-field advantage for PGS000794 (its reported R²=0.439 appears to be full-model and is implausibly high relative to the provided heritability ceiling, so it doesn’t provide clean PRS evidence), the weak-prior ranked top candidate PGS000083 is retained over the strongest runner-up PGS000794.

All candidates are direct matches for rheumatoid arthritis with identical trait_reported/trait_efo and the same phenotyping_reported (Seropositive RA), ancestry setup, cohorts (UKB), covariates=0, and validation size—so this is a near-clone comparison where performance proxies can legitimately break ties. None report PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS004163 has the strongest selected European full-model AUROC (0.7469 vs 0.7283 for the closest runner-up PGS004049) and the highest reported R² (0.1376 vs 0.1220), along with the largest per-SD effect size (OR 2.46 vs 2.37). It also uses an ensemble-style MultiPRS method, which is a positive structural signal versus single-method siblings. Therefore PGS004163 is the best-supported pick over PGS004049.

All candidates are direct matches for prostate cancer with identical phenotype fields, covariates (0), training cohort (UKB), training N (9,671), and the same evaluation context (EUR selected; EVAL includes EUR/SAS; validation n=171,474) from the same publication family—so this is a near-clone comparison where performance proxies can legitimately break ties. PGS004155 has the strongest reported discrimination among the siblings (full-model AUROC 0.7049 and R² 0.1280) and the strongest effect size (OR per SD 2.166), exceeding the closest runner-up PGS004139 (AUROC 0.7003, R² 0.1213, OR 2.109) and PGS004042 (AUROC 0.6994, R² 0.1202, OR 2.112). With no PGS-only AUC/R² available for any candidate, these within-family metric and OR advantages make PGS004155 the best-supported pick.

PGS000922 is the best direct-match for generic sarcoidosis with the strongest clean, PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PRS-only AUROC=0.64282 and PRS-only R2=0.01741 (no-covariates), with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a large evaluation sample (n=67,425). The main runner-up, PGS000923, has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2 but is explicitly a time-to-event (TTE) endpoint, which is a mild endpoint mismatch versus the target’s generic disease status; the small metric edge is not enough to outweigh the cleaner endpoint fidelity of PGS000922. The other candidates (PGS001872, PGS002084) are mapped to skin sarcoidosis and lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r), making them less directly comparable and less endpoint-faithful for the target trait.

PGS000903 is the strongest direct-match Parkinson’s disease PRS in the shortlist because it comes from the large, disease-focused Lancet Neurology PD GWAS meta-analysis family and, within that near-clone family, shows better discrimination and richer PRS signal than its closest sibling PGS000902 (full-model AUROC 0.692 vs 0.651, plus variance explained R²=0.054 and a strong OR top vs bottom quartile=6.25). Both use the same basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and same validation size (n=999), so the performance gap is a legitimate tie-break. PGS001774’s higher AUROC (0.80) is heavily discounted because it is bundled with multiple non-genetic risk factors including family history and other exposures, making the metric less indicative of standalone PRS quality. The remaining candidates (PGS003763, PGS000123) are much sparser and/or lack comparable discrimination metrics, despite large evaluation N for PGS003763.

All candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder cancer (same trait_reported/trait_efo), and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we fall back to comparable full-model metrics under basic covariates. PGS000723 shows the highest reported AUROC (0.583, EUR) versus the strongest runner-up PGS000613 (0.571) from the PRSweb set; covariates for PGS000723 are also minimal (genotyping array only), reducing concern that AUROC is covariate-driven. While PGS000613 has slightly stronger effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.301; top 1% vs rest OR 2.91) and similar basic covariates, its AUROC is lower and the candidates are otherwise close; given the performance-oriented objective, the higher AUROC with clean covariate context makes PGS000723 the best-supported pick.

All candidates are broadly on-trait for retinal detachment, but PGS001137 is the strongest direct-match on visible PRS-comparable performance: it reports PRS-only AUROC=0.573 and PRS-only R2=0.00663 (both below the local h2_obs ceiling ~0.0042 in observed scale terms but in the plausible small-effect range), whereas the higher-ranked portability-paper candidates (PGS002040/PGS001833) provide only partial correlation (0.0276/0.0218) with no PRS-only AUROC/R2, making external performance ranking less supported. Against the closest runner-up with comparable metrics (PGS000990), PGS001137 has clearly better PRS-only AUROC (0.573 vs 0.542), PRS-only R2 (0.00663 vs 0.00213), and incremental AUROC (0.0185 vs 0.0061), while also having cleaner endpoint wording (retinal detachment vs time-to-event retinal detachments and breaks).

PGS005217 is the strongest direct-match for the target (peripheral vascular disease) because it targets the clinically core entity (peripheral artery disease; EFO peripheral arterial disease) with an incident PAD endpoint and is from a disease-focused multi-cohort study with broad multi-ancestry evaluation (validation n=304,294). It also provides stronger performance proxies than the portability-framework alternatives: a C-index/full-model AUC of 0.731 with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a strong per-SD HR=1.66, consistent with meaningful PRS signal. The closest runner-up on label exactness, PGS002055 (peripheral vascular disease, unspecified), comes from a UKB portability framework and shows only a very small partial correlation (0.0175) with no AUC/R2/effect-size support, suggesting weaker predictive utility despite exact trait_efo match. PGS005158 is PAD but restricted to type 2 diabetes with heavy clinical covariates and a weak HR (1.13), making it less suitable as a general PVD PRS.

PGS003586 is the most direct match to the target trait (trait_reported and trait_efo both preeclampsia; phenotyping is pre-eclampsia/eclampsia) and comes from the disease-focused Nat Med multi-cohort study. No candidates report PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect size is the main performance proxy: PGS003586 shows a stronger per-SD association (OR 1.31) than its closest same-study sibling PGS003587 (OR 1.20) under essentially identical covariates and EUR evaluation, making it the better-supported likely higher-performing choice. PGS004593 has weaker endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported gestational hypertension) and a smaller effect size (HR 1.16), despite larger validation N.

PGS000135 is the strongest direct-match schizophrenia candidate within the coherent Am J Psychiatry study family (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported and same basic covariates), and it has a clear performance advantage over the closest siblings: highest reported AUROC (full-model) at 0.74 (vs 0.64 for PGS000136 and 0.60 for PGS000133/PGS000134) under comparable covariate adjustment, plus similarly genome-wide PRS-CS construction with high variant count. PGS002785 is excluded as a non-endpoint match because its phenotyping_reported is cognitive function rather than schizophrenia diagnosis, and its partial R² is not comparable for schizophrenia risk prediction.

All candidates are direct matches for squamous cell carcinoma with EUR-only evaluation and no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so we fall back to within-endpoint performance proxies and near-clone comparisons. Among the three near-clone Cancer PRSweb siblings (PGS000461/PGS000465/PGS000463) with identical covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs1-4) and same training cohort (MGI), PGS000461 has the best reported discrimination and fit (full-model AUROC 0.599 and Nagelkerke R² 0.0304) versus PGS000463 (AUROC 0.593; R² 0.0268) and PGS000465 (AUROC 0.589; R² 0.0282). Although PGS000731 shows a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.605) and large validation N, its covariates are unknown and training/sample details are less transparent, making that small AUROC edge less reliable as a PRS-quality proxy. Therefore PGS000461 is the best-supported direct-match choice over the strongest runner-up PGS000731.

All three candidates are direct matches for the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ‘Carcinoma in situ of skin’), from the same publication, with identical EUR-only ancestry context, training cohort (MGI), validation size (n=5,500), and the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any, the best performance proxy is the comparable full-model metrics and effect sizes within this near-clone set. PGS000471 shows the strongest discrimination and effect evidence versus the closest runner-up PGS000470: higher AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154), higher OR per SD (1.401 vs 1.308), and higher top-1% vs rest OR (3.77 vs 2.45). PGS000469 is clearly weaker on these same metrics (AUROC 0.524; OR per SD 1.09). Therefore PGS000471 is the best-supported choice.

All candidates are concept-aligned to ulcerative colitis, but PGS001307 has the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence in the shortlist: it reports the highest PGS-only AUROC (0.63847) and PGS-only R² (0.02383) among the models that provide clean no-covariate metrics. The closest runner-up is PGS001306, which is also endpoint-matched and reports PRS-only metrics, but is weaker on both PGS-only AUROC (0.63006) and PGS-only R² (0.02036). PGS004253 is disease-focused and shows a strong OR (1.84), but only provides a full-model AUROC (0.66) rather than PRS-only metrics, making it less comparable for performance-oriented ranking; the remaining portability-study scores (PGS001855/PGS002066) have weaker/less informative performance fields (partial-r only or low AUROC/OR).

All three are on-trait, but PGS001791 is the strongest direct-match package for pulmonary fibrosis because it targets the clinically specific endpoint idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and comes from a large multi-biobank, cross-cohort PRS effort using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto, 910,439 variants), which is structurally more likely to generalize than the pan-trait UKB sparse framework score. Versus the main runner-up PGS001030 (pulmonary fibrosis, snpnet, 51 variants), PGS001030 does report higher PRS-only metrics (PGS-only R2=0.0142; AUROC(no covars)=0.625) but it is explicitly from a pan-trait '813 traits in UK Biobank' framework and extremely sparse, a known underperforming archetype in external validation; PGS001791 still provides a clean PRS-comparable R2 (covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only R2=0.005929) with a much more robust genome-wide construction and broader development context. PGS004695 is also IPF but is a 23-SNP GWS score with no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported (only an HR high-vs-low quintile), making it less benchmark-predictive than PGS001791’s explicit PRS-only R2.

PGS001536 is the only candidate with clean PRS-comparable performance reported for vitiligo (PGS-only AUROC=0.64193; PGS-only R2=0.01621), with basic covariates and a large evaluation sample (n=67,425) plus multi-ancestry evaluation records. Its PRS-only R2 is also well below the vitiligo heritability ceiling (h2_obs~0.17), supporting metric plausibility. The strongest runner-up on endpoint fidelity is PGS000738 (trait_reported Vitiligo), but it has an incoherent phenotyping_reported field ('Red hair') and only a small pseudo R2 (~0.039) without PRS-only metrics, making its evidence package less reliable. PGS000760 is explicitly off-target in phenotyping (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), so it is not a direct vitiligo endpoint despite the label.

PGS001795 is the only shortlist candidate reporting a PRS-comparable metric (pgs_only_r2=0.001948; Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out), which is the cleanest available proxy for external benchmark performance and is plausible under the provided uterine-cancer heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0116). It is also a direct endpoint match (phenotyping_reported: uterine cancer) with large European evaluation (n=170,276) and a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with high variant count. The strongest runner-up, PGS003381, has a closely aligned dominant-subtype endpoint (uterine endometrial carcinoma) and a higher full-model AUROC (0.761), but lacks any PRS-only metric and its AUROC is likely largely covariate-driven (age/PCs), making it less reliable as a standalone PRS performance indicator than PGS001795’s explicit PRS-only R2.

All candidates are on-trait (sleep apnea/obstructive sleep apnea), but PGS005219 and PGS005220 are the strongest disease-focused multi-cohort scores (FinnGen + MGBB + MVP) using a genome-wide shrinkage approach with ~983k variants, which is structurally stronger than the MVP genome-wide-significant hit scores (PGS003857/PGS003858; 18/6 variants) and far stronger than the ExPRSweb framework score (PGS003213) that shows weak discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.527). Between the two near-clone 2025 EBioMedicine siblings (PGS005219 vs PGS005220), both report the same full-model AUROC (0.79) with similar covariates and validation size, so the tie-break is the stronger PRS effect size: PGS005219 has a materially higher OR (1.98 vs 1.53), indicating stronger genetic signal. BMI adjustment in the label is not a disqualifier here given the target is generic sleep apnea and OSA is the dominant clinical form.

All candidates are direct matches to type 2 diabetes mellitus and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we fall back to structural signals plus non-inflated performance proxies. PGS002308 is a disease-focused trans-ancestry PRS (PRS-CSx) with genome-wide coverage (~1.26M variants) and explicitly diverse evaluation ancestries, which is a strong transportability/robustness signal for external benchmarks. The strongest runner-up is PGS001781, which shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.852) but it is for an incident endpoint and comes from a risk-factor integration context where the AUROC is likely more covariate-driven and not PRS-comparable; its per-SD OR (1.52) is also weaker than PGS002308’s OR (1.96). PGS004923 is an ensemble MetaGRS (a positive structural signal) but is explicitly framed as integrated clinical risk prediction and has lower full-model AUROC (0.777) with no PRS-only metrics, making its apparent performance less attributable to the PRS itself. The two 582-variant GWAS-hit scores (PGS000804/PGS000805) are structurally weaker for a highly polygenic trait despite similar full-model AUROC (~0.825).

All candidates are broadly on-trait for urolithiasis/urinary calculus/nephrolithiasis, but PGS001250 is the only shortlist entry with explicit PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.56681 and PGS-only R2=0.00592) in a European validation, giving it the strongest direct performance proxy for external benchmark ranking. The top-ranked portability candidates (PGS002075, PGS001864) match the trait well but report only partial correlation (0.0385 and 0.0323) and no AUROC/R2, making their predictive strength harder to compare. The 2024 Commun Biol scores (PGS004563, PGS004493) are also endpoint-aligned but appear to be risk-factor metaPRS/integration variants with only modest per-SD ORs (~1.28 and ~1.23) and no discrimination metrics, so they provide weaker performance evidence than PGS001250’s PRS-only AUROC/R2.

All candidates are direct matches for thyroid carcinoma (trait_efo=thyroid carcinoma; phenotyping is thyroid cancer/incident thyroid cancer) and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on within-family performance proxies and covariate comparability. Among the four near-clone Cancer PRSweb scores (PGS000630/631/632/633) with identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4) and similar sparse architectures, PGS000631 shows the strongest discrimination/effect evidence: highest full-model AUROC (0.636 vs 0.626/0.618/0.628), highest Nagelkerke R2 (0.0478 vs 0.0393/0.0365/0.0447), and the largest per-SD OR (1.651 vs 1.598/1.568/1.609). The main alternative with much higher full-model AUROC (PGS000797, AUROC 0.701) is from a pan-cancer risk-factor integration setting with incident-only endpoint and includes BMI plus broader PCs/array covariates, making its full-model metrics less comparable to standalone PRS performance; it also lacks a clear training sample and is a reweighted variant set. Therefore the best-supported direct-match PRS candidate is PGS000631.
